title: Grow Capital With K Projects
statement:
You start with capital w and can finish at most k projects, one after another. Project i can only be started if your current capital is at least capital[i]. Finishing it adds profits[i] to your capital; the required capital is not spent, it is only a threshold.

Each project can be done at most once. Return the largest capital you can end with.

examples.why: Only project 0 is open at first: capital becomes 1. Now projects 1 and 2 are open; take the one paying 3.
The 5 is locked at the start. Two small projects raise the capital to 2, which unlocks it.
Nothing is affordable, so the capital stays at 1.

hints: Capital never goes down. Once a project is affordable, does it ever become unaffordable?
So at every step, among the projects you can currently afford, which one should you pick? Can picking it ever block a better plan?
Sort projects by required capital. Keep a max-heap of profits for the unlocked ones: before each pick, push every newly affordable project, then pop the largest profit.

explain.intuition:
Two facts make greedy safe. Capital only grows, so the set of affordable projects only grows. And every project adds a non-negative profit. So at each step, the most profitable affordable project is never a mistake: it gives the highest capital now, which unlocks at least as much as any other choice would, and any project you skip stays available for later.

The work is in finding that project quickly. Sort projects by required capital and walk a pointer along them as your capital grows, pushing each newly unlocked profit into a max-heap. Each round pops the top of the heap. Every project is pushed and popped at most once.
steps: Pair each project's capital with its profit and sort by capital.
Repeat up to k times: move the pointer forward while the next project's capital is at most w, pushing its profit into a max-heap.
If the heap is empty, stop: nothing is affordable and nothing will become affordable.
Otherwise pop the largest profit and add it to w.
pitfalls: Taking the highest-profit project overall instead of the highest affordable one. It may not be startable yet, as in the second example.
Subtracting the required capital when starting a project. It is only a threshold.
Rescanning every project each round. That is O(k × n), up to 10¹⁰ steps.

complexity.time: O(n log n + k log n)

solutions.title: Rescan every round
solutions.idea: Each round, scan all unused projects for the most profitable affordable one.

solutions.title: Sort by capital + max-heap of profits
solutions.idea: Unlock projects in order of required capital; the heap always hands over the best affordable profit.
solutions.time: O(n log n + k log n)

followups: Projects can lose money (negative profit). Does the greedy still work?
You can run two projects at the same time and both need the threshold at the moment they start. What changes?
